definition: Preference learning is a subfield of machine learning that focuses on modeling and predicting preferences based on observed preference information.
details: Preference learning typically involves supervised learning using datasets of pairwise preference comparisons, rankings, or other preference information.

explainer.lead: Preference learning models what people prefer rather than what is objectively correct, so systems can rank or choose options from human judgements. It matters because many real tasks, from recommendations to model alignment, only have comparative human feedback.

tiers.eli5: Instead of saying how good each pizza is, you just say which of two pizzas you like more, and the computer learns your taste from those choices.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train on datasets of pairwise comparisons, rankings, or other preference information, typically using supervised learning over pairs. A common pitfall is that pairwise data gives no absolute scores, so scales and consistency across annotators must be handled carefully.
tiers.paperLevel: Preference learning is a subfield of machine learning that models and predicts preferences from observed preference information, usually via supervised learning on pairwise comparisons, rankings, or similar data.

explainer.example: You show a model thousands of pairs of answers and mark which one is better; the model learns to score new answers so the preferred ones rank higher.
